name: @panoptes/cli
//: The build deviates from the root esbuild defaults (CODING.md, Build targets) because its output is not something node runs from this checkout: `deno compile` turns it into the executables a release attaches (docs/release.md).

bundle with thirdParty inlines every workspace package and every npm dependency, so the executable carries no node_modules. format esm because deno reads a bare .js file as an ES module. esbuild.config.mts stamps the workspace version in, which no static option can express.

declaration false so the build writes nothing but its bundle and assets. Nothing reads a declaration it would emit: `deno compile` takes dist/main.js and the directory beside it, and the typecheck emits its own under out-tsc/app. Unset, the executor infers declaration from composite, and the tsc it runs then writes declarations into dist and a near-empty build info over the typecheck's, which is the entanglement issue #146 removed. The type check itself stays: the executor runs it with composite cleared, which is what tsconfig.app.json writes declaration out for.

test depends on this project's own build, not only on its dependencies, because main.spec.ts runs the bundle the build writes rather than the source (issue #33). Without the edge the spec reads whatever dist/main.js was left from an earlier run, or none at all. The root's ^build and ^test are repeated because a leaf dependsOn replaces the default rather than adding to it, and ^test is kept rather than dropped: render.spec.ts and main.spec.ts read four goldens under test-data/render that @panoptes/render writes, and those two and validate.spec.ts read test-data/panoptes/ecluse.yaml and threat-modelling/panoptes.yaml, both of which @panoptes/formats writes back as file snapshots. This project depends on both packages, so the default's mechanism reaches every one of those writes (CODING.md, Build targets). The price is CI's second run of this suite, described below, which now re-runs every dependency suite uncached.

PDF output compiles the Typst source @panoptes/render writes, through that package's pdf subpath, which declares the Typst WebAssembly compiler and reads no file (issue #210). esbuild inlines the module's JavaScript through that import, but the .wasm file itself is read at run time, so esbuild.config.mts copies it and the fonts into dist/assets and scripts/package-cli.sh hands that directory to `deno compile --include`. src/pdf.ts is what reads them back and hands the bytes over, which is why the module is resolved from the package that declares it rather than from this one.

The second runner main.spec.ts uses, the deno-compiled executable in dist/cli, is no nx input: dist/cli is gitignored, so it can be neither a fileset input nor a task output, and nx replays a cached result whether or not that runner took part. Run scripts/package-cli.sh and then `pnpm nx test @panoptes/cli --skip-nx-cache` after recompiling. CI runs that command with PANOPTES_COMPILED_RUNNER=required, which fails the suite where the executable is missing.
